# Guidelines on Veterinary Telehealth

26 November 2025

Guidelines on veterinary telehealth in Singapore

The Animal & Veterinary Service (AVS) and Singapore Veterinary Association (SVA) support the use of technology to provide remote/virtual veterinary care, while ensuring that animal health and welfare standards are upheld, with responsible practice.

A new set of guidelines jointly developed by AVS and SVA provides a resource for veterinarians, pet owners and members of the public on veterinary telehealth. These guidelines serve to set the boundaries, identify areas of risk, and offer guidance on how to practice veterinary telehealth safely in the interest of animal welfare, health, and safety, giving confidence to both veterinarians and clients, if and when they employ veterinary telehealth.

# Oncology - Cancer Management

Image: About Singapore Veterinary Emergency and Specialty Hospital

## Specialist Cancer Care for Pets

A cancer diagnosis in your pet can feel overwhelming – but just like in human medicine, specialised care can make all the difference. At VES Hospital, Singapore’s only veterinary oncologist offers tailored, advanced and compassionate care to improve your pet’s quality of life.

## Singapore’s Only Veterinary Oncologist

Dr Danielle Gibson leads our oncology service with cutting-edge cancer diagnostics and treatments for common cancers in dogs and cats:

  * Lymphoma
  * Mast Cell Tumours
  * Mammary Gland Tumours
  * Nasal Tumours
  * Lung Tumours
  * Liver and Pancreatic Tumours
  * Haemangiosarcoma
  * Melanoma
  * Osteosarcoma
  * Squamous Cell Carcinoma
  * Anal Gland Carcinoma

Advanced imaging like ultrasonography and CT scans are available on-site through our specialist radiology team for accurate diagnosis and staging.

## Integrated Surgical Oncology

Our veterinary specialist surgeons works closely with our oncology team to deliver rapid, high-precision tumour surgeries.

  * Tumour Removal & Biopsy – State-of-the-art surgical techniques and equipment to diagnose and excise tumours with minimal discomfort.
  * Collaborative Treatment Approach – Surgery combined with chemotherapy or other therapies for the best results.
  * Post-Surgical Recovery & Support – Focused on surgical techniques that prioritise pain management and rapid healing to maintain quality of life.

Our multidisciplinary approach ensures your pet receives the most comprehensive cancer care available in Singapore.

## Chemotherapy That Puts Pets First

Unlike in humans, chemotherapy for pets is designed to minimise side effects. Most pets experience little to no discomfort and can continue eating, playing, and enjoying life.

Our oncologist, Dr Danielle Gibson, will be able to offer the following:

  * Personalised Treatment Plans – Tailored chemotherapy protocols for your pet’s specific cancer type.
  * Effective, Pet-Friendly Treatments – Designed to minimise side effects while ensuring optimal treatment of your pet’s cancer.
  * Quality of Life for your Pets – Our focus is always on ensuring your pet is happy, comfortable, and pain-free, even while receiving chemotherapy.

## Frequently Asked Questions

What happens during an oncology appointment?

Your first visit helps us understand your pet’s condition and build a personalised treatment plan.

You can expect:

  * Review of Your Pet’s Medical History – Our oncologist will go through your regular clinician’s referral notes and ask about symptoms, previous diagnostics, and your concerns.
  * Physical Examination – A full physical check, with special focus on any abnormal growths or areas of concern.
  * Diagnostics Discussion – We may recommend further tests such as bloodwork, fine needle aspirates, biopsies, X-rays, or advanced imaging (e.g., CT scan) to confirm diagnosis and staging. There are, however, no obligations to proceed with any further diagnostics if you choose not to.

A veterinary oncologist is a cancer specialist – like an oncologist in human medicine. They undergo years of additional training focused on diagnosing and treating cancer in animals. From designing chemotherapy plans to managing complex or advanced cases, they work closely with your regular vet to provide a coordinated, expert-led treatment plan.

How long will my pet need to be on cancer treatment?

The duration of treatment depends on the cancer type, stage and the treatment plan. Some pets may only need a few sessions, while others may continue for several months. Our oncologist will discuss a clear timeline with you during the initial consultation.

Will my pet lose their fur or feel sick from chemotherapy?

Most pets tolerate chemotherapy much better than humans. Hair loss is rare, and side effects like nausea or fatigue are usually mild and temporary, if they occur at all. We closely monitor your pet and adjust treatment to keep them as comfortable as possible.

## Connect with a Singapore Vet from Malaysia

Singapore and Malaysia share a love for pets. They also face similar challenges when it comes to caring for their pets. That's why many Malaysian pet parents are turning to Pawlyclinic for help via teleconsultation.

Why we are special !

With a teleconsultation, pet parents can seek advice from a vet without having to travel. This is especially helpful for those who live in remote areas which have limited access to veterinary care. Telemedicine also offers the benefit of flexibility, as teleconsultations can be scheduled at a time that is convenient for both the pet parent and the vet.
Thanks to the power of telemedicine, our vets are able to provide vital support and guidance to those who need it anytime, anywhere. However, please bear in mind that telemedicine does not replace in-clinic care but rather complements it. Pets will always have a need to see their vet in-person for a physical examination but an online vet can serve as the first responder and advise you accordingly. 

How much do online vets cost?

The vets and vet clinics on our platform set their own consultation fee; and it starts from SGD $35 (or ~ MYR 112) per consultation per pet. When you log into the pet parent portal, you will see the list of vets and vet clinics as well as their respective rates. You can also filter the list of vets and vet clinics by their consultation fee to narrow down to just those who fall within your budget.

Are online vets legit?

All our vets must have a valid veterinary license from The Animal & Veterinary Service (AVS) and extensive hands-on, in-clinic experience. In order to practice on Pawlyclinic, vets undergo a review process to ensure that they are qualified to deliver the best care to pets via our platform.

## Limitations of Teleconsultations

There are several conditions or situations in veterinary medicine that may not be suitable for teleconsultation and require in-person evaluation and treatment.

## Emergency Cases

  * Severe trauma, such as car accidents or major injuries.
  * Acute respiratory distress.
  * Severe bleeding.
  * Sudden collapse or loss of consciousness

## Diagnostic Procedures

  * X-rays, ultrasounds, or other imaging studies that require specialized equipment.
  * Laboratory tests, such as blood work or urine analysis.
  * Biopsies or cytology for further evaluation of lumps or masses.

## Physical Examinations

  * Palpation of internal organs or assessing for specific physical signs.
  * Neurological examinations that require hands-on assessment of reflexes and coordination.
  * Evaluating skin conditions, wounds, or lumps that need direct examination.

## Procedures and Treatments

  * Surgeries or surgical consultations.
  * Dental procedures, such as cleanings or extractions.
  * Administration of vaccines or injections that require veterinary supervision.
  * Wound care that needs cleaning, debridement, or suturing.

## Behavioral Assessment

  * Assessing complex behavioral issues that may require observation of the pet in its environment.
  * Developing behavior modification plans that need direct interaction with the pet.

## End-of-Life Care

  * Compassionate euthanasia decisions and support for pet owners.
  * Palliative care planning for terminally ill pets.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can a vet diagnose my pet online?

A teleconsultation allows a veterinarian to assess your pet’s condition based on your description, medical history, photos, and videos. However, some conditions require an in-person examination or diagnostic tests to reach a definitive diagnosis.

### Can I get a prescription through a teleconsultation?

No. Prescription medications can only be provided after a veterinarian has physically examined your pet.

### How long does a teleconsultation take?

Most consultations take approximately 15 to 30 minutes, depending on the complexity of your pet’s condition.

### What should I prepare before my appointment?

If available, prepare any relevant medical records, photographs, videos of symptoms, medications that your pet is taking and a list of your concerns. A stable internet connection and a well-lit area for your pet are also helpful.

## Personalised, Compassionate Oncology Support for Veterinarians
